b1-unit-13.13.1 A call to Dr. Ana:
Ana: Hi Danny! I got your message. How are you feeling?
Danny: Terrible. I woke up on Tuesday with a sore throat, and now I feel awful. I've got a headache, my whole body aches, and I keep sneezing. I've been coughing a lot, too, especially at night.
Ana: Have you got a temperature?
Danny: I think so. I feel hot and cold at the same time. Mrs. Lima checked, and it was thirty-eight point nine.
Ana: Hmm. Any breathing problems? Or an upset stomach?
Danny: No, my stomach is fine. I can breathe, but my nose is completely blocked.
Ana: OK. It sounds like the flu, not a cold. A cold usually starts slowly and it's milder. The flu hits you suddenly, with a high temperature and body aches.
Danny: Great. So what should I do? Bruno has some antibiotics from last year. He says I ought to take them.
Ana: No! You'd better not take them. Antibiotics only work on bacteria, and the flu is a virus. They won't help you at all. If I were you, I'd stay in bed for a few days and drink lots of water. You can take something for the fever and the aches, and a decongestant might help with your nose.
Danny: Got it. What about my throat? It really hurts.
Ana: Why don't you ask Mrs. Lima for some tea with honey? Throat lozenges help, too. And you ought to eat something, even if you're not hungry.
Danny: Mrs. Lima has already made me soup. Twice!
Ana: Of course she has! Now, you're a tour guide. Have you got any tours this weekend?
Danny: Yes, on Saturday. Two of them.
Ana: Then you'd better call Carla today and cancel. You need to rest, and you don't want to give the flu to twenty tourists.
Danny: You're right. I'll call her. Oh, and speaking of injuries... Bruno twisted his ankle at the running group on Sunday. It's really swollen.
Ana: Poor Bruno! He should put an ice pack on it and keep his foot up. And he'd better not run for a couple of weeks.
Danny: He won't be happy. Thanks, Ana. You're the best doctor in São Paulo.
Ana: You're welcome. But listen, if you have any breathing problems, or if the fever doesn't go down in three days, you should see a doctor in person. Promise?
Danny: I promise. Bye!
